# Research Discrepancies

Conflicts between sources, and claims that need verifying. The AI logs them here so work isn't blocked, and they
get resolved later. Tracked in git, but not published (`docs/scratch/**` is excluded from the site).

## How to help resolve (you + AI)

1. **Pick an entry** and do what its **To settle** line says (usually a Training Mode lab), or find a better
   source.
2. **Add your findings under that entry** as a `- **Notes (you):**` bullet. Rough notes are fine, eg "labbed
   2026-10-02 vs Mario, stale OFF: nair early 14.4% → 12 base". Longer lab write-ups go in
   `docs/scratch/lab/<YYYY-MM-DD>_<topic>.md`: link it from the entry, and it counts as a source (`Lab:` in
   Sources dropdowns).
3. **Tell the AI** "resolve D-00X" (or "review discrepancies" to go through all open ones). It reads your notes
   and then:
   - updates the affected places listed under **Affects** (docs pages, SmashDb notes, code constants)
   - records the **Resolution** with evidence and date
   - flips the page pointers (`% research: discrepancy D-00X (resolved)`)
   - updates code built on the changed pages (tagged `docs-source:` in code) and re-runs the tests
   - adds an eval case when it's a fact the AI could get wrong again
4. **Disagree with a provisional value?** Say so in your notes. It will be revisited in the same pass.

**Conventions (for the AI):**
- IDs are never reused.
- Statuses: `open` → `needs-lab` → `resolved` / `wont-fix`. Resolved entries stay as history.
- Types: `conflict` (sources disagree) / `unverified` (single source, or derived, and needs checking).
- Every entry gets a **Provisional** value so work can continue. Rules for picking it are in
  `.agents/skills/smash-research/SKILL.md` ("Discrepancies").
- Put entry-specific ideas for verifying in **To settle**, and shared setup in "Lab basics" below.
- This file is read in an editor, not published, so plain pipe tables are fine here (unlike site pages).

(lab-basics)=
## Lab basics (Training Mode)

Most entries are settled by reading exact damage numbers in Training Mode. The shared setup:

| Setting | Why |
|---|---|
| **Stale Moves: OFF** | Every hit deals listed damage (no freshness `1.05×`, no staling). Turn it ON only when testing staling |
| **2+ CPUs**, or divide by `1.2` | Turns off the 1v1 multiplier (1 CPU = 1v1 = `1.2×` damage) |
| CPU standing still, low percent | Consistent hits. Percent doesn't change damage, only knockback |
| Damage readout | Shows each hit's exact damage. It's the only reliable cue: no visual or sound marks a multiplier (short hop vs full hop aerials differ only in jump height) |

**How to run a test:**
- **Predict first:** write the expected number for each outcome before labbing (eg listed × `0.85` vs listed
  × `1`), so one reading tells you which claim holds.
- **Change one thing at a time**, eg only the jump type, same move and hitbox.
- **Repeat each case 2–3 times** to rule out a mistimed input or a different hitbox connecting.
- **Record the setup** in your notes: characters, CPU count, stale moves on/off, exact inputs, readings. Eg
  "2026-10-02, DK vs Mario, 2 CPUs, stale OFF: FH nair 12.0, SH nair 10.2".

## D-004 — SL Armour sheet stale counts · status: open · type: conflict

- **Affects:** Straight Lunge armor "stales needed" results; any comparison against the sheet
- **Claims:**
  - Stale Moves rules ([SmashWiki](https://www.ssbwiki.com/Stale_Moves), `docs/mechanics/stale_moves.md`): the
    1.05× freshness bonus applies only when the move isn't in the queue. So 14 base damage is tanked by
    uncharged SL after **6** stales, and 15 after **7**
  - SL Armour sheet: **7** and **8** respectively. Its numbers match keeping the freshness bonus (and using a
    ×1.25 "1v1 + freshness" factor instead of 1.2 × 1.05 = 1.26) even after staling
- **Why they might differ:** a formula shortcut in the sheet. It doesn't state its formula, but "1v1 +
  freshness damage (base × 1.25) × (1 − reductors) ≤ 9.6" reproduces every row of the DK tab, so it keeps the
  freshness bonus after staling (checked in `tests/ds/calc/test_little_mac.py`). Rows where our result differs,
  as base damage → ours vs sheet: 9.35 → 2 vs 3, 12.75 → 5 vs 6, 13.6 → 6 vs 7, 14 → 6 vs 7, 15 → 7 vs 8,
  16 → 8 vs 9, 17 → 9 vs "Unarmorable"
- **To settle:** stale a 14-damage move 6 times (eg DK down B) and check whether uncharged SL tanks it
- **Provisional:** Stale Moves rules (sourced mechanic over numbers derived from a spreadsheet)
- **Resolution:**

## D-008 — Short hop aerial damage multiplier · status: needs-lab · type: unverified

- **Affects:**
  - `docs/moveset.md` (`sl-armor-modifiers` table)
  - `docs/glossary.md` ("Short hop attack" row)
  - code built on those rows: `docs-source:` tags in `pkgs/ds/calc/modifiers.py` and
    `pkgs/ds/calc/little_mac.py`, plus the tests in `tests/ds/calc/`
- **Claims:**
  - **0.85× applies to aerials performed in a short hop, in Ultimate:**
    - [SmashWiki: Short hop](https://www.ssbwiki.com/Short_hop), Ultimate paragraph of "Mechanics" (revid
      2038420): "Short hop aerials have a 0.85× damage modifier"
    - [SmashWiki: Peach (SSBU)](https://www.ssbwiki.com/Peach_(SSBU)): "The new 0.85× damage multiplier for
      aerial attacks performed in a short hop … her float bypasses the multiplier"
    - [SmashWiki: Recoil damage](https://www.ssbwiki.com/Recoil_damage): recoil is "affected by the 0.85× short
      hop damage multiplier" (Ultimate context: Inkling ink, spirits)
    - the SL Armour sheet's short hop rows are exactly listed × 0.85
  - **0.85× is only for Smash 64:** user research, 2026-09-30 (source not recorded)
  - **Our current docs and code:** 0.85× only for jump + attack "short hop attacks", 1× for other short hop
    aerials. This was an over-narrow reading of the Short hop page
- **Notes (you):** 2026-09-30: researched, and the 0.85 multiplier looks like it's only for Super Smash Bros. 64.
- **Notes (AI):** 2026-09-30:
  - The Smash 64 `0.85` on the Short hop page is in the "Short hop heights" table (Giant Donkey Kong row). That's
    jump height, not damage, so it's a likely source of the 64-only reading.
  - There's no double jump damage multiplier. The "air jump multiplier" on the Double jump page is also a jump
    height value.
  - "IDJ gets a multiplier" is really **avoiding** the short hop reduction. Once you double jump you're no longer
    in the short hop, so aerials deal full damage. The same goes for Peach's float (stated on her page). IDJ
    itself isn't stated on the wiki pages checked.
  - **Inputs that give a short hop** (so aerials during them deal 0.85×):
    - tap jump and release within the 3-frame jumpsquat
    - press two jump buttons together (since 2.0.0)
    - press jump + attack together ("short hop attack")
  - Only the jump type matters, not timing: an aerial on the first airborne frame and one just before landing
    should both be 0.85×. This is an inference, and the lab below checks it.
  - Only **aerials** are affected. Tilts, jabs and smashes after landing are full damage.
- **To settle** (see [Lab basics](#lab-basics)): DK early nair, listed `12.0`, 2+ CPUs, stale moves OFF,
  2–3 reps each.

  | Case | Input | Expected if 0.85× (Ultimate) | Expected if 1× |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Full hop nair | hold jump, then nair | `12.0` | `12.0` |
  | Short hop nair (tap) | tap jump, nair | `10.2` | `12.0` |
  | Short hop attack | jump + attack together | `10.2` | `12.0` |
  | Short hop nair, late | tap jump, nair just before landing | `10.2` | `12.0` |
  | IDJ nair | short hop, double jump immediately, nair | `12.0` | `12.0` |
  | Ground tilt after landing (control) | land, then ftilt (listed 8.0 / 9.0) | `8.0` / `9.0` | `8.0` / `9.0` |

  - **Short hop cases read `10.2`:** the Ultimate 0.85× is confirmed. Late equal to early means there's no
    timing window. IDJ at `12.0` means IDJ avoids it.
  - **Short hop cases read `12.0`:** no short hop reduction in Ultimate (the 64-only reading).
- **Provisional:** 0.85× for jump + attack short hop attacks only (current docs/code), until resolved.
- **Proposed resolution (awaiting user OK + lab):**
  - short hop aerials (any input) deal 0.85× in Ultimate
  - full hop, double jump / IDJ and Peach float aerials deal 1×
  - rename the "short hop attack" variant and glossary row to "short hop aerial"
  - replace the "normal short hop" modifiers row with "full hop / double jump / IDJ / Peach float: 1×"
- **Resolution:**
